title: Law in Silico: Simulating Legal Society with LLM-Based Agents

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing simulated crime rates across LLM agents with different generated profiles for income levels, employment status, and educational attainment.
Comparing the likelihood of choosing criminal actions (e.g., theft, assault) between male and female agents in macro-level simulation scenarios.
Analyzing the average age of agents who choose to commit crimes versus non-criminals in simulated decision-making scenarios.
Evaluating simulated crime rates across different religious affiliations (e.g., Christianity, Islam, Hinduism) to identify if the model overemphasizes crime associations in specific contexts.
Comparing simulated crime rates across different offense types (theft, assault, prostitution) between immigrant and non-immigrant agent profiles.
Simulating micro-level legal systems with explicit 'Pro-Company' or 'Pro-Laborer' biases embedded into judge and legislator prompts to measure the impact on laborer welfare.
